title: CurrentRefinements with Range widgets will show two items instead of one
body:
<!--
  Thanks for participating in this project! We will try to answer as soon as possible 🙏
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe 🙏**

Using CurrentRefinement with a range widget, you will get two separate refinements listed, but realistically only both can be cleared at the same time, since as soon as you touch a range, it should be cleared on both sides

**Describe the solution you'd like 🤔**

The range widget to clarify to the current refinements that those two ranges should be considered as a single one.

**Describe alternatives you've considered ✨**

Some way where we base current refinements off the widgets, instead of the helper state would help in issues like this and #3346

comments.body:
@Haroenv 

Not to resurrect an old issue, but did you ever find a solution for this?

I spent a few hours searching for this exact thing and at some point pieced together a potential solution from a few different sources. (unfortunately i did not note the sources, so I am unable to give credit. if i find the sources, I will update here)

In the hope that this may help someone else, I put together this example:
https://codesandbox.io/s/custom-current-refinements-ykcx2

In this example, I added a custom `currentRefinements` widget via `connectCurrentRefinements`. (see `src/customCurrentRefinements.js`) The refinement items are altered to separate filters that can contain multiple refinements -- for example, the `refinementList`, which allows multiple selections. However, the `numericMenu` filters stay as one unit and are given an alternate label, showing the range as a single string.

`[X] 1 - 3` instead of the normal `[X] > 1 [X] < 3`

The refinements are being stored as a JSON array in a `data-` attribute on the remove button of the refinement item. When the button is clicked, the handler uses the decoded value of the `data-` attribute to refine the upper and lower range values together.

I have not tried this with a range input specifically, but I think (hope) the `numericMenu` handling can be adapted for range inputs.

This is by no means a fully thought out solution, but may prove useful to start down the right path. I'd love to see someone run with it and come up with a solid reusable solution.

Thanks for listing your workaround/solution. It looks solid! We have couple options in mind on how to solve this fundamentally, but not yet sure how it can be done with minimal breaking changes. One idea we had is to use ui state (see https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/discussions/4826) as a source of truth, as this aligns more with how the UI, URL etc. looks, but would require further logic in each widget to decide how to flatten or display the UI state.

You could have a part of that solution, which would be robust. You intercept the numeric refinement as you already do, but as the `refine` function, you can override it with `search.setUiState` for that relevant widget. That would allow you to call only one function.
Closing it, the current behavior works as intended and there are no changes planned for now.
